analysis.title: markets / macro (Tony Pasquariello, 14 Nov 2026)
key_insights: Pasquariello's directional framework is positive for the rest of 2026 and more complicated for 2027. Equal weight S&P closed 11/13 about 1% below its all-time high, and NDX rose 3.5% on the week.

The week's index gains came despite the bellwether stock of the AI era losing over $500bn of market cap and a 33 bps rise in the US 2-year yield on inflation concerns. Daily rotations have been severe for leveraged traders.

Near-term support for 2026: flows after position cleansing, seasonals (since 1952 the last seven weeks of the year are up 69% of the time, average +2.1%), continued AI demand (TSMC and CRWV cited), and nominal US GDP growth running above trend and accelerating in H2.

2027 risks: US politicians may disrupt the AI infrastructure buildout, more regulation and higher taxes are possible, core inflation is sticky and the latest CPI suggests it is broadening, and 2027 may see the largest increase in net supply since 2000 (exhibits 6 and 14).
Counterpoint: NDX is trending to be up in 17 of the past 18 years on total returns, and sturdy GDP growth supports earnings growth and the broad uptrend.

Conclusion: risk is positively skewed through year-end and the primary trend in the S&P remains higher. Into 2027 he expects more volatility, less upward convexity and lower risk-adjusted returns, a 'seesaw' with modest gains.

Positioning: since the start of October the trading community has liquidated a large share of net and gross exposure. Last week GS saw its biggest sale of global AI stocks in four years, and net exposure across the PB book is in the 3rd percentile of the past year.
Corporate supply-versus-demand for stock should improve meaningfully as November progresses.
Other points: responses to last week's note on US credit market concerns were mostly negative in tone, and the US economy has never been more sensitive to stock market performance (exhibit 11).
Chart view: the Dow Theory primary trend of the S&P is higher, and Q2 2026 was something of a mini bubble.

sector_views.rationale: The week was volatile for AI infrastructure stocks, with the biggest sale of global AI stocks in four years at the GS franchise. TSMC and CRWV show demand remains strong. Political and regulatory risk to the buildout rises into 2027.

earnings_insights: The report says healthy GDP growth supports earnings growth. It cites TSMC and CRWV as evidence of AI demand but gives no EPS or revenue figures.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The rise was attributed to inflation concerns, yet NDX still rallied 3.5%.

macro_indicators.reading: Running above trend and appearing to accelerate in H2 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports earnings growth and the broad bull trend. The acceleration was not expected.

macro_indicators.reading: Sticky, and the latest CPI report suggests it is broadening
macro_indicators.interpretation: Central bank tightening of liquidity is the main risk to the bull market.

Pasquariello expects more volatility and less upward convexity into 2027.

geopolitical: US midterm elections are behind the market. The report flags 2027 political risk, with US politicians potentially disrupting the AI infrastructure buildout and bringing more regulation and higher taxes.

tension_points.bull_case: Positive skew through year-end: position cleansing supports flows, seasonals are strong (up 69% of years since 1952 over the last seven weeks, +2.1% average), AI demand is strong and nominal GDP growth is above trend. NDX is on track to be up in 17 of the past 18 years.
tension_points.bear_case: 2027 brings political risk to the AI buildout, more regulation and taxes, sticky and broadening core inflation, and the largest net supply increase since 2000. Expect more volatility and lower risk-adjusted returns.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A central bank that chokes off liquidity. The report says bull markets die for that reason rather than from old age, and it names no specific level.
